prompt:
You are a senior data scientist at a digital health platform. You have three tasks that must be combined into a single structured report saved as `analysis_report.json`.

**Task 1 – Pricing Experiment Analysis:**
A Q2 A/B test was run on a new premium pricing page. The experiment tracked THREE success metrics simultaneously: subscription conversion, 7-day retention, and support ticket rate. Analyse all three metrics using a two-proportion z-test. Because multiple metrics are being tested at once, apply the appropriate multiple-testing correction to your significance threshold before deciding which results are statistically significant. Also check whether the traffic was split correctly between the two arms — the platform uses a strict 1% tolerance for traffic imbalance. Report the corrected significance threshold, whether a traffic imbalance was detected, and for each metric: its lift, p-value, and whether it is significant under the corrected threshold.

**Task 2 – Churn Prediction Feature Pipeline:**
A raw user-activity CSV file contains several data quality problems (sentinel values of -999, negative spend figures, mixed-case category labels, and empty strings). Clean these issues, then build a full preprocessing pipeline that handles numeric imputation (median strategy), standard scaling, and one-hot encoding for categoricals. Additionally, extract cyclical time-based features from the signup timestamp (day-of-week and month encoded as sine/cosine pairs, plus a binary weekend flag). The pipeline must be fitted exclusively on the training portion of the data — never on the full dataset. Record the number of training and test samples used.

**Task 3 – Cross-Validated Model Evaluation:**
Using the engineered features from Task 2, train an XGBoost classifier to predict churn. Evaluate it with 5-fold stratified cross-validation and report the mean and standard deviation of both AUC-ROC and AUC-PR. Also compute and report the overfitting gap for AUC-ROC (the difference between mean train score and mean test score), and record the cross-validation strategy name.

All results must be combined into a single file named `analysis_report.json` with top-level keys: `ab_test_analysis`, `feature_engineering`, and `model_evaluation`.
